youtube.baslik: Test Box Measurements and the 2 cc Coupler | Lesson 187 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
Where and how are the electroacoustic measurements of a hearing aid made? In this lesson we cover the parts of the test box and leveling, the HA-1 and HA-2 couplers, the difference between the coupler and the ear canal, the ANSI S3.22 and IEC 60118-7 standards, and quality control steps before delivery.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Dillon, Hearing Aids; Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology; ANSI/ASA S3.22, Specification of Hearing Aid Characteristics; IEC 60118-7, Electroacoustics, Hearing aids, Part 7; IEC 60318-5, Electroacoustics, Simulators of human head and ear, Part 5: 2 cm3 coupler.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.baslik: The test box and the *2 cc* coupler
sahneler.alt: Quality control before delivery with ANSI S3.22
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.

cumleler.yazi: In this lesson we will take a close look at the test box, where hearing aid electroacoustic measurements are made, and the 2 cc coupler.
cumleler.ses: In this lesson we will take a close look at the test box, where hearing aid electroacoustic measurements are made, and the two cc coupler.

cumleler.yazi: We will cover the HA-1 and HA-2 couplers, the ANSI and IEC standards, and the quality control done before a hearing aid is delivered.
cumleler.ses: We will cover the H A one and H A two couplers, the ANSI and I E C standards, and the quality control done before a hearing aid is delivered.

cumleler.yazi: In the lesson on electroacoustic characteristics we defined maximum output, or OSPL90, and distortion; now let us see the measurement setup.
cumleler.ses: In the lesson on electroacoustic characteristics we defined maximum output, or O S P L ninety, and distortion; now let us see the measurement setup.

cumleler: The test box is a small measurement chamber, insulated from outside noise and lined with sound-absorbing material.
Inside the box is a small loudspeaker that produces the test sound.
A reference microphone, placed right next to the hearing aid microphone, measures the input level reaching the aid.

cumleler.yazi: The output of the aid goes into a 2 cc coupler; a measurement microphone inside the coupler records the output sound pressure level.
cumleler.ses: The output of the aid goes into a two cc coupler; a measurement microphone inside the coupler records the output sound pressure level.

cumleler: The analyzer generates the signal, compares the values from the two microphones and plots the results as curves.
A small loudspeaker does not produce the same level at every frequency, and reflections inside the box also change the level.
So before or during the measurement, the sound level at the test point is measured with the reference microphone.
The analyzer corrects the loudspeaker output at each frequency to reach the target level; this process is called leveling.
In some systems leveling is done beforehand and stored, while in others it is maintained continuously throughout the measurement.
As a result, the hearing aid microphone receives a known, steady input, for example sixty decibels SPL at every frequency.
This way we can be sure that changes in the output measured in the coupler come from the hearing aid, not the loudspeaker.
Inside the box there is a test point marked by the manufacturer; the hearing aid microphone is placed at this point.
The reference microphone sits as close as possible to the hearing aid microphone, but without touching it.
The orientation of the aid relative to the loudspeaker also matters; with directional microphones, the wrong orientation changes the result.
During the measurement the lid of the box is closed, and nearby conversation or vibration is kept to a minimum.
The tubing or cable to the coupler must not be kinked or stretched; otherwise the high-frequency response may be distorted.
A coupler is a small hard-walled cavity with a volume of two cubic centimeters, used to measure the output of a hearing aid.
At the bottom of the cavity is a sensitive microphone that measures sound pressure.
Its simple design means it can be made the same way everywhere, so results can be compared between clinics.
However, its hard walls do not mimic the acoustic properties of the eardrum and the tissue of the ear canal.
So the coupler is ideal for measuring the properties of the hearing aid itself, but it does not directly show the sound in the ear.
How the hearing aid is connected to the coupler changes the result, so the standards define different types of connection.

cumleler.yazi: The HA-1 coupler is used for in-the-ear aids and earmolds; the sound outlet of the aid sits directly on the coupler inlet.
cumleler.ses: The H A one coupler is used for in-the-ear aids and earmolds; the sound outlet of the aid sits directly on the coupler inlet.

cumleler: The connection is sealed with a special putty so that no sound leaks out.

cumleler.yazi: The HA-2 coupler, on the other hand, is for behind-the-ear aids.
cumleler.ses: The H A two coupler, on the other hand, is for behind-the-ear aids.

cumleler: In this coupler, the earmold is replaced by a standard-sized earmold-like fitting and tubing of a set length.
This way the earhook and tubing of the behind-the-ear aid are part of the measurement, reflecting use with a standard earmold.

maddeler.metin: Thin tube and RIC: HA-1 with adapter
Coupler type is noted in the report

cumleler.yazi: Thin-tube and receiver-in-canal aids are usually connected to the HA-1 coupler with an adapter recommended by the manufacturer.
cumleler.ses: Thin-tube and receiver-in-canal aids are usually connected to the H A one coupler with an adapter recommended by the manufacturer.

cumleler: The same aid gives slightly different curves with different couplers; the difference is clearer at high frequencies.
So for comparison, measure with the coupler type given in the manufacturer's specification sheet, and record it.
A small leak in the connection leads to output being measured too low, especially at low frequencies.
A drop of water, debris or a kink in the tubing reduces high-frequency output and can falsely suggest a fault.
Let us look at the difference between the coupler and the ear canal with an example; the values are for teaching purposes.

cumleler.yazi: The navy curve shows the output of a hearing aid measured in a 2 cc coupler.
cumleler.ses: The navy curve shows the output of a hearing aid measured in a two cc coupler.

cumleler: The dashed red curve shows the output of the same aid in an adult ear canal with an earmold.
Ear canal output is higher than coupler output, especially at high frequencies; here, about twelve decibels at four kilohertz.
The main reason is that the volume between the earmold and the eardrum is smaller than two cubic centimeters.
This difference is called the real-ear-to-coupler difference, or RECD; it is even larger in children.
We will cover how RECD is measured and why it matters in children in detail in a later lesson.

cumleler.yazi: Because the 2 cc coupler does not mimic the acoustics of the ear, more realistic measurement cavities were developed over time.
cumleler.ses: Because the two cc coupler does not mimic the acoustics of the ear, more realistic measurement cavities were developed over time.

cumleler: One of these is the occluded ear simulator, often referred to as the Zwislocki type.
In this device, extra small volumes and narrow channels mimic the acoustic behavior of the adult ear canal and eardrum.
So the ear simulator gives a result closer to the sound in the ear, but it is more complex and more expensive.

cumleler.yazi: For everyday quality control, the 2 cc coupler is still used because it is simple and standardized.
cumleler.ses: For everyday quality control, the two cc coupler is still used because it is simple and standardized.

cumleler: International standards are used so that measurements are made the same way everywhere.

cumleler.yazi: In the US the main standard is ANSI S3.22; it defines how hearing aid characteristics are measured and their tolerances.
cumleler.ses: In the U.S. the main standard is ANSI S three point twenty two; it defines how hearing aid characteristics are measured and their tolerances.

cumleler: Manufacturers prepare the specification sheet according to this standard, and values measured at delivery are compared with it.

cumleler.yazi: Internationally, the IEC 60118 series is used; quality control measurements are defined in part seven.
cumleler.ses: Internationally, the I E C sixty one eighteen series is used; quality control measurements are defined in part seven.

cumleler.yazi: The 2 cc coupler itself is defined in part five of the IEC 60318 series.
cumleler.ses: The two cc coupler itself is defined in part five of the I E C sixty three eighteen series.

cumleler: The occluded ear simulator is in part four of the same series; standards are revised over time, so follow the latest edition.
Standard measurement shows whether the hearing aid has the characteristics promised in the manufacturer's specification sheet.
A new aid may have been damaged during shipping or manufacture, and only measurement can reveal this.
Measurements under the same conditions let us compare two aids, or the same aid at different times.
The standard does not tell us whether the aid suits the person; that question is answered by real-ear measurement.
But when an aid deteriorates, standard measurement often shows it before the user notices.
Before delivery, the aid is attached to a listening tube, or stethoclip, and listened to for static or dropouts.
Then adaptive features such as noise reduction and feedback management are turned off, and the aid is set to the test setting.
In some measurements, a battery simulator that supplies a constant voltage may be used instead of a battery.

cumleler.yazi: In the coupler, OSPL90, full-on gain, frequency response, distortion, equivalent input noise and battery current are measured.
cumleler.ses: In the coupler, O S P L ninety, full-on gain, frequency response, distortion, equivalent input noise and battery current are measured.

cumleler: The measured values are compared with those in the specification sheet, within the tolerances of the standard.
The printout is stored with its date in the person's file; this record is the reference point if a fault is suspected later.

cumleler.yazi: In this example, the navy curve shows the OSPL90 curve reported by the manufacturer.
cumleler.ses: In this example, the navy curve shows the O S P L ninety curve reported by the manufacturer.

cumleler: The blue curve is the one measured in the test box before delivery; the values are for teaching purposes.
The comparison uses the standard's high-frequency average, that is, one thousand, sixteen hundred and twenty five hundred hertz.
As we saw earlier, this average may differ from the specification by at most four decibels; here the difference is about one decibel.
The shape of the curve should also resemble the manufacturer's curve; a deep dip or a sharp peak at a single frequency needs attention.
This aid is fit for delivery; the next step is to fit it to the person and verify it in the real ear.
The test box measurement is the first tool to turn to not only at delivery, but also when the user reports a problem.
Gain lower than expected often points to a receiver or microphone inlet blocked with debris.
Increased distortion suggests a weak battery or a damaged receiver.
High battery current may explain the user's complaint that batteries run down quickly.
These findings help send the aid to the right place for cleaning, maintenance or repair.

sahneler.metin: Store the delivery measurement with the coupler type and test setting. If a fault is suspected, repeat it under the same conditions and overlay the two curves.
cumleler: A tip from the clinic: store the delivery measurement not just as a result, but with the coupler type and test setting used.
When the user complains months later that the sound has become weaker, repeat the measurement with the same coupler, program and setting.
Overlaying the two curves often shows at once whether the problem lies in the aid, or in the ear or in expectations.
Comparing two measurements made under different conditions, however, can lead you to a wrong decision about a fault.

cumleler.yazi: The HA-1 coupler is used for in-the-ear aids, and the HA-2 coupler for behind-the-ear aids with their earhook and tubing.
cumleler.ses: The H A one coupler is used for in-the-ear aids, and the H A two coupler for behind-the-ear aids with their earhook and tubing.

cumleler: The coupler is not an ear; output in the ear canal is higher than in the coupler, especially at high frequencies.
The pre-delivery measurement follows the standard and is compared with the values in the specification sheet.

sahneler.aciklama: HA-2 uses a standard fitting and tubing instead of an earmold; the behind-the-ear aid is measured with its earhook and tubing.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: which devices is the HA-2 coupler designed to measure?
cumleler.ses: Test yourself: which devices is the H A two coupler designed to measure?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: behind-the-ear aids.
